newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SICOM says changes in rubber contract from Nov 1.
newsitem.headline: SICOM says changes in rubber contract from Nov 1.

text.p: The Singapore Commodity Exchange (SICOM) said on Tuesday that changes in its TSR20 rubber contract will be implemented beginning on November 1.

* SICOM Said in a statement that trading in the October/December 1997 contract months will be on FOB terms only and that trading in the current TSR20 award contract will last until the July/September 1997 contract months.

"The TSR20 (FOB) contract will provide tremendous cost savings for traders," SICOM said. "With the better and more consistent quality of TSR20 produced these days, there is no longer any need to inspect and test every lot of TSR20 as is stipulated in the award system."
* The new TSR20 rubber contract will be denominated in U.S. dollars against the previous Singapore dollars.
"Hedging will be easier as the physical trade is conducted in U.S. dollars, so there will be no need to compare the U.S. dollar and Singapore dollar prices and no foreign exchange risks," SICOM said.

* The acceptable unit will be in 20.16 tonnes of TSR20 rubber from SICOM's approved list of factories. The previous system used units of 20.16 or 19.20 tonnes of TSR20 delivered to SICOM for previous testing.

* The TSR20 rubber in the new contract must meet the technical specifications of the country in which the factory is located in say Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia or Singapore. Under the old system, SICOM set minimum specifications.

* Packaging will use shrink-wrap instead of the former wooden pallets. The method of delivery will be at the warehouse or FOB at buyer's option in Singapore port instead of the former negotiable award certificates.

* Buyers need not pay a premium for awarding/warehouse cost. SICOM said this would make exchange prices better reflect physical TSR20 prices making the contract more attractive for hedging and trading.

* Alternative delivery procedure (ADP), which was barred under the old contract, will now be allowed, SICOM said. ADP will make delivery more flexible, enabling buyers/sellers who are matched to arrange mutually beneficial private terms at negotiated premiums/discounts, it added.
This might involve, for example, delivery direct from source port or alternative grades of TSR such as TR5 or TSR10.
* Members of SICOM will enjoy a 10 percent concessionary tax for income derived from trading in TSR20 (FOB) contracts, it added.
SICOM said the proportion of TSR in dry rubber production is increasing at the same time as the usage of RSS (Ribbed Smoked Sheet), as the main rubber for tyres, is declining.

TSR consumption is also expected to grow, given the tyre industry's preference for natural over synthetic rubber, and with 75 percent of natural rubber being used in the tyre industry, the exchange added.
